description: The bar chart illustrates the distribution of experts across 24 layers in a Layer-wise Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architecture, as described in the paper “Less, but Better: Efficient Multilingual Expansion for LLMs via Layer-wise Mixture-of-Experts.” The vertical axis, labeled “Number of Experts,” ranges from 0 to 10 with tick marks at integer intervals, indicating the total number of experts assigned per layer. The horizontal axis, labeled “Layer,” lists layers 1 through 24. Each bar is a stacked column composed of three segments: a blue base representing a shared expert component, a green middle segment labeled “G1,” and a yellow top segment labeled “G2.” The legend confirms these color assignments. The total height of each bar reflects the sum of experts per layer, varying from 3 to 9. For example, Layer 1 has 9 total experts (1 blue + 4 green + 4 yellow), while Layers 11–15 each have 3 total experts (1 blue + 1 green + 1 yellow). The chart reveals a non-uniform allocation strategy: early layers (e.g., 1–5) and later layers (e.g., 19–22) tend to have more experts, particularly in the G2 group, while middle layers (e.g., 10–15) are more sparsely populated. This visual pattern suggests a deliberate, layer-dependent expert allocation designed to optimize multilingual efficiency by concentrating capacity where it is most needed.
